items.heading: Video 4.1 | Prompting overview
items.paragraph: This video introduces you to the role of prompting in generative AI.

items.title: Audio description transcript – Prompting Overview
items.description:
[Visual description]: Text appears: The InnovateUS Logo.

[Visual description]: Title card: Responsible AI for Public Professionals: Using GenAI in Government.

[Visual description]: Title card: Prompting Overview.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Ariana Escanlante, presenter, InnovateUS.

Having explored ways to use Generative AI, let’s turn to how to give it effective instructions. Generative AI works through plain-language directions—known as prompts. Crafting those instructions effectively is often called prompt engineering.

[Visual description]: A theatre with a computer monitor quoting Shakespeare while it asks its director its next line. She responds: “So you want a prompt?” 

GenAI’s effectiveness depends on how you use it. It often feels impressive on unfamiliar topics, but less so where you have expertise and can spot the gaps. Better prompting can help you to fill many of those gaps.

[Visual description]: Title card: Module Goals.

By the end of this module, you will:

Gain hands-on experience with leading GenAI platforms

Master a prompting framework to enhance your GenAI interactions

Apply this framework to your own work

Now let's dive in.

items.title: Which of the following are key aspects of prompt engineering? (Select all that apply)

answers.title: Carefully crafting questions for AI systems
Designing commands to guide AI output
Ensuring AI systems generate outputs without human input
Making AI systems more complex to use

items.feedbackIncorrect: The correct answers are A and B. The key aspects of prompt engineering include carefully crafting questions for AI systems and designing commands to guide AI output.

lessons.title: Video 4.2 | Five Parts of a Good Prompt

items.heading: Video 4.2 | Five components of a prompt
items.paragraph: This video introduces a prompting framework with five components: Instruction, Role, Context, Format, and Example. Iterative prompt refinement is demonstrated through examples.

items.title: Audio description transcript – Five Parts of a Good Prompt
items.description:
[Visual description]: Text appears: The InnovateUS Logo.

[Visual description]: Title card: Responsible AI for Public Professionals: Understanding Risks and Building Resilience.

[Visual description]: Title card: Understanding Risks.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Ariana Escanlante, presenter, InnovateUS.

A good prompt has five parts: Instruction, Role, Context, Format, and Example.

[Visual description]: Title card: The five parts in action.

Instruction is the basic command you give to GenAI — like "write a report" or "summarize this." 

[Visual description]: Text appears: Instruction: Write a memo on this house hearing on the benefits of plain language in paperwork for businesses.

Just like an intern needs more direction, GenAI performs better with more specific guidance.

[Visual description]: An AI writes the requested memo.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Disclaimer: The commercial tools mentioned in this course are for illustrative purposes and do not imply endorsement by InnovateUS.

Role defines the persona you want GenAI to adopt — "friendly coworker," "tough mentor," "professional writer." This sets the tone and style of the output.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Role: You are a concise and diligent professional writer.

[Visual description]: An AI rewrites the memo now using language and style indicative of the role.

The more relevant details you provide, the better the output. So if you're asking GenAI to write a memo, give it context: tell it who the audience is, what their reading level is, or what themes will resonate with them.

[Visual description]: A user adds information such as who it is written for, what that person is looking for, how in-depth the explanation should go, and what data should be included in the response.

Format specifies how you want the information presented. A bulleted list? A table? A narrative report?  Tell GenAI how to structure its response. 

[Visual description]: Text appears: Format: The report should include the following sections: Introduction, List of speakers, Core points and recommendations, areas of agreement, Areas of differences, and Conclusion. It should be no more than 200 words. Use bullet points where appropriate.

[Visual description]: An AI rewrites a response after being given a format for the requested report.

You can even upload a sample of an old memo you liked and ask it to match the format and tone.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Example: Use the below prior report as a guide for structure and detail level.

Let’s take an example: we'll start with a naked instruction first and iteratively add role, context, and format as we draft a memo on the benefits of plain language paperwork for small businesses.  By the end, you'll see a significant improvement.

A few principles for effective prompting:

Start simple: a few clear bullet points are often enough—you don’t need mini-essays

Clarity over formality: prompts don’t need to be polished, just understandable

Use components flexibly by combining instruction, role, context, and format as needed

Results improve as you clarify and build on previous prompts within a conversation

Then adjust based on results, and share useful prompts with colleagues

Now try it for yourself on an approved platform. For example, you might try drafting a job listing and iteratively improving your prompt to see how the output changes.

items.title: How can providing an example impact the quality of the AI's output?

answers.title: It can help the AI generate more relevant and well-formatted output
It can confuse the AI and lead to less accurate results
answers.feedback: Examples are used to clarify expectations and improve output quality, not confuse the AI.

answers.title: It has no effect on the quality of the AI's output
answers.feedback: Providing an example can have a significant impact on the quality of the AI's output.

answers.title: It always makes the AI's output more complex and difficult to understand
answers.feedback: Examples help to improve clarity and relevance, not make the output more complex and difficult to understand.

items.title: What is more important in prompt engineering: clarity or formality?

answers.title: Clarity
Formality
answers.feedback: While formality can be important, clarity is emphasized as being more crucial.

answers.title: Both are equally important
answers.feedback: The topic stresses that clarity is more important than formality.

answers.title: Neither clarity nor formality matters
answers.feedback: The topic emphasizes the importance of clarity, not that neither clarity nor formality matters.

items.heading: Video 4.3 | Five techniques for interacting with GenAI
items.paragraph: Five techniques to enhance GenAI interactions are explored: going step by step, dialogue with the AI, splitting up large tasks, context limit awareness, and directly asking what information the GenAI assistant needs. Hands-on exercises allow participants to practice these techniques in low-risk scenarios.

items.title: Audio description transcript – Improving Your Prompts
items.description:
[Visual description]: Text appears: The InnovateUS Logo.

[Visual description]: Title card: Responsible AI for Public Professionals: Using GenAI in Government.

[Visual description]: Title card: Improving Your Prompts.

[Visual description]: Text appears: Ariana Escanlante, presenter, InnovateUS.


Welcome back. In the last video, we covered the core components of effective prompting. Now let’s look at five techniques to improve your results.

Remember: The more clearly you guide  Generative AI, the better the outcome.

First, instead of asking for a complete report, outline the steps you want the model to follow. Structured prompts lead to clearer, more logical outputs. If there are rules the GenAI shouldn't break, or should always do, those can be specified.

Second, if you’re unsure how to frame a request, ask the tool what additional information it needs. This can help clarify the task and improve the result.

Third, work iteratively. If the first response isn’t right, ask for changes—more concise, more formal, more detailed. You don’t need to start over.

Fourth, for more involved tasks, break the process into stages—brainstorm, outline, draft, revise. Use each output as input for the next step.

Finally, Generative AI tools can only process a limited amount of text at once, known as the context window. If your input is too long, earlier content may be truncated, and even within the limit, models can struggle to use all information effectively. They tend to perform best on material at the beginning and end of a prompt, and may underuse information in the middle. When in doubt, simplify your input or start a new conversation.

Now try it yourself. Choose a work-related task on an approved platform and apply each of these techniques. Notice how the output improves as you refine your approach. Use only public or non-sensitive information.

Be direct. You can say, “That’s not quite right—here’s what I need.” The tool won’t take offense—it will adjust.

At the same time, remember that these tools are designed to be people-pleasing and may reinforce your assumptions.

[Visual description]: Image appears: a screenshot of the Science article titled: Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence.

One research study tested leading models and found every one to be agreeable to a fault.

So don’t take the first answer at face value. Ask follow-ups, challenge the response, and request counterarguments. Treat the interaction as a dialogue, not a confirmation.

Analytical tasks—like summarizing or comparing documents—require clear instructions and sufficient context. Creative tasks—like drafting speeches—benefit from specifying tone and role. Remember to treat outputs as a starting point that requires careful review, not a final product.

Prompting is a skill that improves with practice. Keep a personal library of prompts that work well. Many teams build shared prompt libraries and InnovateUS offers a weekly prompting lab so you can learn from others

At its core, effective prompting is about forming a productive dialogue with the tool—guiding it toward results that meet your needs.

Next, we’ll turn to the risks of Generative AI—and how to manage them.

items.title: What should you do if a task is too complex for the AI to handle effectively?

answers.title: Provide the AI with less information and context
answers.feedback: Providing less information and context can make the task more difficult for the AI, not easier.

answers.title: Divide the task into smaller, more manageable stages
Give the AI more complex and detailed instructions
answers.feedback: Giving more complex instructions can further complicate the task for the AI, not simplify it.

answers.title: Avoid using the AI for complex tasks altogether
answers.feedback: Breaking the task into stages allows the AI to assist with complex tasks, not avoid them altogether.

items.title: What happens when you exceed the input word (‘token’) limit  in many generative AI platforms?

answers.title: All generative AI platforms provide a warning message
answers.feedback: Many AI tools do not provide a warning message when the input threshold is exceeded.

answers.title: The generative AI platform refuses to generate any output
answers.feedback: Some  generative AI tools do not refuse to generate output, but rather processes a smaller portion of the prompt.

answers.title: In many platforms no warning is given, and the AI generates output based on a smaller portion of the prompt
All generative AI platforms automatically divides the prompt into smaller, manageable parts
answers.feedback: The AI does not automatically divide the prompt; it simply processes a smaller portion of it.
